report.tagline: An Indian app company that sells cheap subscriptions to audiobooks, audio shows and, through its Kuku TV app, short vertical video dramas in Hindi and other Indian languages.
report.simpleSummary: Kuku FM started as an app for audiobooks and audio shows in Hindi and other Indian languages, on topics from self-help to love stories. In 2024 its parent, Kuku Technologies, launched Kuku TV, an app of micro-dramas: soap-opera stories told in one to two minute vertical video episodes. You watch the first few episodes free and then pay for a subscription, often starting with a very cheap trial that renews automatically through UPI. Kuku TV made the company's revenue jump six times in a year, and it is now preparing to list on the stock market.

overview.whatItDoes: Kuku Technologies runs Kuku FM for audio and Kuku TV for micro-dramas, mainly for Hindi-speaking and regional Indian users. It makes nearly all its money from subscriptions paid through UPI autopay or app stores. It spends heavily on ads on Instagram and YouTube that show a dramatic clip and drop viewers into the app.
howItWorks: A user sees an ad with a cliffhanger clip and installs Kuku TV or Kuku FM.
The first few episodes are free; then a paywall asks for a subscription.
Many plans start with a low-price trial and then auto-renew at a higher weekly or monthly price through UPI autopay.
Kuku TV shows are one to two minute vertical episodes, often romance, revenge or family drama, with a full story in 50 to 100 episodes.
Kuku FM offers audiobooks, audio shows and summaries on self-help, business, spirituality and stories.
The company is investing in AI tools to make content faster and cheaper.
overview.valueProposition: For users: cheap, gripping stories in their own language on a phone, in short bites. For the business: a subscription model that earns money from users directly, instead of relying on low Indian ad rates.

businessModel.summary: Kuku makes almost all of its money from subscriptions: ₹1,475 crore of ₹1,484 crore in FY26. Ads and pay-per-view bring in very little. Most of the money goes back into ads to find new subscribers. It turned profitable in FY26 because revenue grew much faster than costs.

revenueStreams.detail: Weekly, monthly and yearly plans for Kuku TV and Kuku FM, mostly via UPI autopay and app stores. Over 99% of revenue.
One-off purchases of content, ₹6.9 crore in FY26.
₹20.5 crore from outside India, a small but growing share.

businessModel.pricing: Not fully public. Plans often start with a low-price trial and then renew at weekly or monthly prices shown in the app. Prices change by show and offer.
costDrivers: Marketing and ads (₹1,105 crore in FY26)
businessModel.unitEconomics: In FY26, for every ₹100 Kuku earned, it spent about ₹74 on marketing, about ₹5 on staff and about ₹6 on operations, leaving a small profit. So the key question is how long each subscriber stays. If finding a subscriber costs ₹300 in ads and they pay ₹150 a month, they must stay at least two months to break even. Users who sign up for a cheap trial and cancel right away lose money. Users who stay for months make the business profitable.

howTheyGetUsers: Instagram and YouTube ads with dramatic clips
Free episodes at the start of each show
Word of mouth and WhatsApp shares
whatBringsUsersBack: Cliffhangers at the end of each episode
growth.moat: Kuku has a big library of Indian-language content and years of data on which ad clips and stories convert. Its marketing engine is hard to build. But the micro-drama format is easy to copy, and rivals like ShareChat's QuickTV and JioHotstar's Tadka have huge audiences.

competitors.name: Pocket FM
competitors.positioning: Audio series app, now mostly earning in the US with coins.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Kuku earns 99% in India and uses subscriptions; Pocket FM uses pay-per-episode coins.

competitors.name: QuickTV (ShareChat)
competitors.positioning: Micro-drama app that can promote to ShareChat and Moj users.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Kuku spends on outside ads; QuickTV has its own user base.

competitors.name: JioHotstar Tadka
competitors.positioning: Short-format shows inside JioHotstar, with 100 million users in two months.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Kuku is a standalone app; Tadka gets free distribution to 440 million users.

competitors.name: Audible and Storytel
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Kuku FM is cheaper and focused on Hindi and regional content.

competitors.name: YouTube and Instagram Reels
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Kuku sells long stories split into paid episodes.

northStar.metric: Paying subscribers still active after 60 days
northStar.why: As a north star metric, this shows users value the content enough to keep paying, which is what makes the heavy marketing spend pay back.

improvementIdeas.idea: Send a clear reminder 24 hours before the first full-price renewal, with a one-tap cancel button in the app.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users complain about unexpected debits after trials, and regulators are watching dark patterns.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer complaints and disputes, and more trust before the IPO.

improvementIdeas.idea: Offer a per-show pass at a fixed price instead of an auto-renewing plan.
improvementIdeas.problem: Many users want one story, not a subscription.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher conversion from users who avoid autopay.

improvementIdeas.idea: Personalised 'next show' within the last episode of a series.
improvementIdeas.problem: Subscribers leave after finishing one story.

improvementIdeas.idea: Use AI dubbing to launch top shows in Tamil, Telugu and Bengali.
improvementIdeas.problem: Growth is concentrated in Hindi markets.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: New users at lower content cost.

improvementIdeas.problem: Buffering on slow networks in small towns.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Episodes per day in Tier 3 towns

pmLessons: A new format can change a company. Kuku TV micro-dramas grew revenue over six times in one year.
Marketing-led growth is only as good as retention. With ₹74 of every ₹100 going to ads, subscribers must stay to make money.
Easy payments can become a trust problem. UPI autopay boosted sign-ups but also complaints and regulator attention.
In India, users will pay small amounts directly if the content hooks them, which can beat low ad rates.

interviewQuestions.question: Kuku spends about 78% of its costs on marketing. Is that healthy?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain payback: cost to get a subscriber vs how much they pay over time. Ask for retention data. Say when high marketing is fine and when it is a red flag.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce complaints about auto-debit without hurting revenue?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate users who feel tricked from those who forget. Propose reminders, easy cancel and per-show passes. Track refund rate, ratings and long-term revenue.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you compete with JioHotstar's Tadka?
interviewQuestions.hint: Tadka has free distribution. Kuku must win on content, speed and niche genres. Pick a segment and measure share of micro-drama watch time.

interviewQuestions.question: What metrics would investors care about at Kuku's IPO?
interviewQuestions.hint: Revenue growth, subscriber retention, marketing as a share of revenue, profit margin, and revenue concentration in India.

interviewQuestions.question: Design the first-time user experience for Kuku TV.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start from the ad click. Decide how many free episodes, when to show the paywall and what price. Test and measure conversion and first renewal.

We assume most FY26 revenue growth came from Kuku TV, based on news coverage; the company did not split revenue by app.
